raw_response:
I have farmed this land for fifty years. My father farmed before me. I know this soil, I know this county. Two people in my house — my wife and me — we don't need more than we can manage.

All 9 mu rotates between wheat and maize. That is how we have always done it here in Quzhou. Wheat goes in after National Day holiday in October, we harvest it in June, then we plant maize right away. Same land, full 9 mu, twice a year.

**Wheat:** I use the improved variety the county seed station sells — I have used it for many years and it gives me steady yield. I apply compound fertilizer as base before plowing, then urea at jointing stage. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble. I irrigate in November for winter protection, again at jointing, again at heading — three times is enough with my well. I spray herbicide in early spring and fungicide when the ears come out. That is all. I do not experiment at my age.

**Maize:** Hybrid seed, same as everyone around here. No-tillage now — my back cannot manage deep plowing twice a year anymore, and the neighbors say it works fine to direct-seed into the wheat stubble. I apply fertilizer in two splits. Summer rain usually helps but I pump from the well at tasseling and grain fill if it is dry. One herbicide spray early, maybe one more for pests if bad. That has been enough most years.
